name: Keyboard layout map
plain: Reads which character each physical key makes, so the page can tell the keyboard layout.
meaning: The layout map shows if the person types on QWERTY, AZERTY, Dvorak or a language specific keyboard. That narrows country and language, and helps shortcuts, but it is also a fingerprint hint.

access.revocation: Nothing to revoke (no permission is stored)
access.iframe: Permissions Policy keyboard-map (default self); secure context
steps: Promise resolves with a Map of KeyboardEvent.code to character

data.metric: Map of key code to produced character

fields.name: KeyQ
fields.precision: q on QWERTY, a on AZERTY

limits.headline: Can learn which keyboard layout you use, such as QWERTY or AZERTY
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when the page or app loads
can: Check which letter each physical key types
Guess your country or language from the layout
Show shortcuts that match your keyboard
cannot: Show a permission pop up; there is none
limits.differs: Chrome, Edge and Samsung Internet support it. Firefox and Safari do not.

story.what_it_is: The page can tell which keyboard layout you use, which hints at your country or language.

marketing.name: Keyboard API
marketing.pitch: Describes a way for web apps to learn which key sits where, so games and editors can show the right key labels.

story.for_you: You see correct key hints in a game, like 'Press Z to jump' on a French keyboard. You do not see that the site learned your layout. It does not ask.
story.for_makers: Games and shortcut heavy apps need to know which key is where. The same info is a quiet clue to country and language, so fraud and ad systems may add it to a browser profile.

use_cases.example: A browser game shows 'W A S D' hints as 'Z Q S D' for a French player, so controls make sense.
A design or music web app maps shortcut keys by physical position, so shortcuts feel right on any layout.
A web editor shows the right shortcut label such as the correct slash key on German keyboards.
A fingerprinting script uses the layout as one more clue, together with language and time zone.
A fraud tool compares the layout with the claimed country, and a mismatch raises suspicion.
A remapping tool for people with one hand or limited reach uses the layout to build custom shortcuts.

technical_bounds: Chromium only (Chrome 69 and Edge 79); Firefox and Safari do not implement it
Returns about 40 to 50 printable key entries (the alphanumeric block)
Reflects the active layout; changes fire layoutchange events
Page in a background tab may get an empty map
